title: Tag-steered slot reader for strings, pairs and nested brackets
summary: A reader keeps C two-word slots and a few counters. Pair and string tasks are answered from the slots. For nested brackets it uses a boundary tag that arrives with every token: the bracket symbol that opened the innermost constituent still open. A small learned map turns what was read into an output symbol.
core_idea: Answer nested-bracket prefixes from a per-token boundary tag and everything else from a fixed slot store, so nesting needs no growing structure and only a handful of training sequences.

state.name: S
state.meaning: Slot store: row i holds an address and the item written under it; C is a card parameter, set to 64 for the listed sizes.

state.name: f
state.meaning: Fill count: number of slot rows written so far, between 0 and C.

state.name: p
state.meaning: Pending address: the first symbol of a pair whose second symbol has not arrived.

state.name: o
state.meaning: Offset counter: how many symbols have been emitted since the separator.

state.name: beta
state.meaning: Boundary tag beta_t delivered alongside token t by the segmenter: the opening bracket symbol at the left edge of the innermost constituent that is still open after t, or -1.

state.name: Phi
state.meaning: Output map from a read result r to an output symbol, R entries, fitted by tallying.

state.name: mu
state.meaning: Mode setting chosen by learning: 0 pairs, 1 string, 2 tag.

update.latex: \mu=0:\; p=\varnothing \Rightarrow p \leftarrow x_t;\; \text{else } S_f \leftarrow (p, x_t),\; f \leftarrow f+1,\; p \leftarrow \varnothing
update.plain: pairs mode: the first symbol of a pair waits in p; the second one is written with it as row f, then f grows by one (x_t is the token at step t)
update.name: pair write

update.latex: \mu=1:\; t < t_{sep} \Rightarrow S_f \leftarrow (f, x_t),\; f \leftarrow f+1;\quad t > t_{sep} \Rightarrow o \leftarrow o + 1
update.plain: string mode: before the separator (step t_sep) each symbol is written under its position; after it the offset counter o counts emitted symbols
update.name: string write

update.plain: tag mode: nothing is written; the segmenter output Seg(x_1..x_t) is taken as the tag beta_t
update.name: tag intake

readout.latex: r_t = \begin{cases} S[\text{first } i: S_{i,0}=x_t]_1 \text{ chased up to } H \text{ times} & \mu=0\\ S_{o,1} & \mu=1\\ \beta_t & \mu=2 \end{cases},\qquad \hat{y}_t = \Phi[r_t]
readout.plain: read result r: in pairs mode the item stored with the current symbol, followed again while it is itself an address, at most H times; in string mode the item in row o; in tag mode the tag; the output is Phi[r]

learning.description: For each of the three modes and each choice of separator symbol (symbols that occur exactly once in every training sequence), run the reader over the m training sequences, tally the pairs (read result, required output), set Phi by the majority per read result, and keep the mode with the most training outputs right.
learning.few_shot_argument: Only the mode, the separator and Phi are fitted. In tag mode Phi has two entries, so m = 8 sequences fix it at any depth; the other tasks use m = 12 sequences.

complexity.constants_notes: One scan of at most C rows per chase step and at most H steps; 2C + 6 words of state. The tag is read as part of the token.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Mode selection plus a majority map; the tag carries the nesting structure.

prediction.statement: From m = 8 training sequences of two-type bracket nesting at depth 16, the learned reader predicts the legal closer with per-query accuracy at least 0.99.

capabilities.task: copy a string after a separator
capabilities.prediction: String mode copies L = 8, 32, 64 over D = 4 exactly with C = 64 (state 2C + 6 words).
Pairs mode answers every key at K = 8, 32, 64 exactly with C = 64.
Tag mode predicts the legal closer at depth 2, 4, 8, 16 with accuracy 1.0 and a two-entry map.
Pairs mode with H = 2 answers f(g(x)) at T = 4, 16, 32 (C = 64) and with H = 9 resolves chains of 1, 4, 8 hops.

capabilities.task: limit: recall beyond the slot count
capabilities.prediction: The limit is a storage count: C slots of two words cannot hold more than C pairs, so at C = 64 an instance with 65 or more distinct pairs loses one of them.

known_relatives.name: not assessed
known_relatives.relation: This card does not compare its mechanism with others.
known_relatives.claimed_difference: No difference from earlier work is claimed.

falsifiers: A training set of 8 depth-16 bracket sequences after which the closer accuracy is below 0.99.
A recall instance with K <= C distinct pairs that the pairs mode answers wrongly.

toy_example.description: Tag mode on one depth-3 bracket word: tags come from a scan, Phi maps opener to closer.
